taxonomy.label: processes
taxonomy.description: Fundamental carrier-flow capabilities the tool can represent, defined by their mathematical role rather than by named technologies. `Carriers` are the energy or non-energy commodities that flow between processes (e.g. electricity, heat, hydrogen, CO2, water, materials). Only physical processes are in scope; decision-making agents are `actors`.

members.label: conversion
members.description: Carriers are transformed into other carriers within the system boundary (e.g. power plants, electrolysers, heat pumps, CO2 capture). This enables coupled multi-carrier optimisation.

members.label: explicit demand
members.description: Carriers are consumed within the system boundary by explicit processes with their own balances and constraints, rather than by a fixed exogenous profile parameter.

taxonomy.label: network
taxonomy.description: Network physics representation beyond the `processes.spatial_transfer` baseline, where flows are coupled by the physics of the transporting medium rather than by capacity limits alone.

members.label: power flow
members.description: Electrical network representation beyond the `processes.spatial_transfer` baseline.

members.label: hydraulic flow
members.description: Pressure-driven network representation for carriers transported through pipes, beyond the `processes.spatial_transfer` baseline (e.g. methane, hydrogen, CO2, district heat/cooling, water).

taxonomy.label: asset
taxonomy.description: Representation of the individual assets that make up the system: how their capacities are represented, how their operation is resolved, and the costs they incur. Limits on asset investment and operation, and the mathematical form those limits take, are `constraints`.

members.label: capacity representation
members.description: How asset capacities can be represented in the model and optimisation problem.

members.label: operating representation
members.description: The resolution of asset operation representation in the model. A linearised approximation of unit commitment is `tractability.reformulation.linearised_unit_commitment`.

members.label: cost
members.description: Asset investment and operating cost representation. Cost which varies linearly with a decision variable (e.g. EUR/MW capital cost on nameplate capacity, EUR/MWh operating cost on flow) is the baseline; we do not track it explicitly here.

taxonomy.label: constraints
taxonomy.description: Limits on asset investment and operating decisions, and reliability requirements imposed on the system as a whole, whether enforced as hard constraints or as penalty costs. `scope` describes what a limit spans; `functional_form` describes the mathematical form of the relationships between decision variables that the tool can express.

members.label: scope
members.description: What a limit spans: the regions, assets, or time periods that a constraint links or applies within.

members.label: functional form
members.description: The mathematical form of the relationships the tool can impose between decision variables, and hence the problem class handed to the solver. A linear relationship between an input parameter and a single decision variable (e.g. a fixed efficiency applied to a flow, resource availability scaled by capacity) is the baseline; we do not track it explicitly here. Non-linear and quadratic terms in the objective are instead `asset.cost.nonlinear` / `objective.quadratic`.

members.label: path dependent
members.description: Constraints in which a quantity evolves endogenously based on cumulative historical decisions, rather than from input parameters alone. Approximating this by pre-generating vintaged components is instead `model_definition.component_templating`.

members.label: reliability
members.description: Reliability requirements imposed as constraints or penalty costs within the optimisation, under deterministic inputs. Post-hoc adequacy assessment is `postprocessing.probabilistic_reliability_assessment`; probabilistic decision methods are `uncertainty`.

taxonomy.label: model definition
taxonomy.description: How the model's parameter space and dimensions can be shaped, grouped, and reused, independent of any single parameter, constraint, or cost.

taxonomy.label: math
taxonomy.description: Access to, and user extension of, the underlying mathematical formulation.

taxonomy.label: interface
taxonomy.description: Available options for users and machines to drive the tool: defining, configuring, and structuring a model (`build`); executing a model run (`run`); interacting with model outputs (`analyse`); plus tool-level execution and solver configuration.

members.label: gui
members.description: Graphical user interface.

members.label: api
members.description: Programmatic interface (e.g. language API, web API).

members.label: cli
members.description: Command line interface.

members.label: visualisation
members.description: Built-in rendering of model inputs or outputs as visual artefacts, independent of whether a `gui` is available to interact with them.

taxonomy.label: io
taxonomy.description: Data formats, conventions, and mechanisms for moving model input/output data. Computing new parameters is `preprocessing`.

members.label: plain text
members.description: Data in human-readable, diff- and version-control-friendly text formats (e.g. CSV, JSON, YAML).

members.label: binary
members.description: Data in compact / compressible, non-human-readable binary formats (e.g. Excel, NetCDF, HDF5, Parquet).

members.label: database
members.description: Data in databases (relational or otherwise).

members.label: remote storage
members.description: Data can be read from / written to remote storage (e.g. object stores, cloud drives).

members.label: lazy loading
members.description: Data can be loaded lazily / out-of-core, allowing datasets larger than memory.

members.label: standardised
members.description: Accepts or emits data following a community-recognised convention or ontology (e.g. Open Energy Ontology <OEO>, IAMC template, the Energy System Description Language <ESDL>, Common Energy System Model <CESM>, SiennaSchemas), including standardised network-data formats (e.g. PSSE RAW, matpower case files, Common Information Model <CIM>).

taxonomy.label: edge effects
taxonomy.description: Distortive effects of system boundaries and linearising model components can be mitigated against. Flows across the spatial boundary are `processes.boundary_exchange`.

taxonomy.label: actors
taxonomy.description: Representation of heterogeneous decision-making actors, deviating from the single, central-planner baseline.

taxonomy.label: pathway
taxonomy.description: Foresight extent and planning direction across operational (intra-annual) or investment (inter-annual) time periods. A single-snapshot run — "overnight" capacity expansion, or dispatch without a time dimension - is the baseline; we do not track it explicitly here.

members.label: perfect foresight
members.description: Perfect foresight capacity expansion / dispatch.

members.label: myopic foresight
members.description: Time periods are optimised sequentially, with each decision made without knowledge / with limited knowledge of later periods.

taxonomy.label: objective
taxonomy.description: Objective-function options beyond minimisation of a single linear cost term.

taxonomy.label: uncertainty
taxonomy.description: Methods that restructure the decision problem to account for parametric or structural uncertainty.

taxonomy.label: tractability
taxonomy.description: Approaches to reduce the computational cost of building and solving the problem, trading exactness for speed.

members.label: dimension reduction
members.description: Options to reduce the size of a given dimension of the problem.

members.label: reformulation
members.description: Approximations of discrete or non-linear formulations that preserve (mixed-integer) linear tractability.

taxonomy.label: orchestration
taxonomy.description: Tool-managed workflows coordinating multiple complete runs in series/parallel, where the result emerges from the ensemble or its convergence.

taxonomy.label: preprocessing
taxonomy.description: Options to generate parameters derived from user-defined input data before running the model. Moving/storing data is `io`.

members.label: spatial distribution
members.description: A user-defined parameter can be automatically distributed spatially using other spatial parameters.

taxonomy.label: postprocessing
taxonomy.description: Postprocessing analyses that can be triggered by the tool based on model outputs, on a per-asset or system-wide basis.

members.label: impact assessment
members.description: Auxiliary impacts calculated from model outputs.

members.label: operational
members.description: Operational analyses derived from model outputs.

members.label: financial
members.description: Financial analyses for business cases, derived from model outputs.

members.label: network transfer metrics
members.description: Network transfer capability and flow-sensitivity metrics derived from model outputs.

members.label: probabilistic reliability assessment
members.description: Probabilistic resource-adequacy metrics calculated post-hoc. Sampling-based run orchestration to produce them is `orchestration.sampled_runs`.

taxonomy.label: transparency
taxonomy.description: Transparency of the modelling pipeline: logs, diagnostics, and traceability of data as it moves through the workflow.

members.label: metadata propagation
members.description: Metadata is propagated from inputs through to outputs.

useCases.name: Bidding Zone Review
useCases.description: Model impact on energy system design, systemwide costs, and / or transmission system congestion of implementing new market mechanisms or updating existing ones. This could include bidding zone reviews; direct subsidies; feed-in-tariffs; contract auctions.
assumptions: The optimization will be run over individual years with myopic foresight over days or weeks within the year.

Available transmission lines are set by scenarios from the network development plan (NDP), are limited between bidding zones using power transfer distribution factors, and are represented using security-constrained AC optimal power flow.
Generator capacities are fixed by the integrated resource plan (IRP).

Assets are resolved individually where possible and their unit commitment as well as economic dispatch is represented with the aim of accurately representing the day-ahead and intra-day markets. This may require iterating between an optimisation and simulation run to resolve bidding decisions.
Only the power system is considered.
The system supply-demand balance is relaxed. Load shedding is limited with constraints on EENS and LOLP applied alongside a value of lost load (VOLL).

Resilience to weather uncertainty is addressed using multi-stage stochastic optimisation applied across rolling horizon windows. This may require decomposing the problem into different optimisation problems that are iterated upon until convergence.
Users require a GUI to navigate model preparation, optimisation, and analysis.

useCases.name: Integrated Resource Planning (IRP)
useCases.description: Create a set of high-level scenarios of e.g. 2050 decarbonised energy system designs for use in guiding policy implementation, creating procurement plans, and providing boundary conditions for investors, utilities, and local authorities to develop their own plans. Future scenarios account for full sector coupling and GHG emission accounting.
assumptions: The optimization will be run with perfect foresight over the full model horizon, which spans multiple years/decades.

Investment decisions may occur once every N (> 1) years.
 Within a year, the timeseries is contiguous but may be resampled.
Large assets (e.g. thermal power plants, hydro) are individually resolved; distributed assets (e.g. wind & solar) are grouped per project or region.
Large assets are represented with unit commitment due to operating constraints which require resolving (ramping, uptimes, run ups. etc.).
Hydro cascading and technology chaining internal to power plants is not represented.
Generator contract arrangements (e.g. min/max dispatch obligations) are represented.
Technology economies of scale and bidding levels are represented.
Hydro storage levels are set by the model at the start/end of the time horizon.
Demand-side flexibility is represented by time-shiftable loads.
LOLP/EENS constraints are not explicitly set; the standard system balance constraint will set this to effectively zero energy not served.
Curtailment rates are calculated in post-processing.
Robustness and MGA techniques will not be employed. Sensitivity analysis will be limited to a small set of tests and therefore not require monte carlo techniques.
There is sufficient computational capacity to run the model with defined spatio-temporal scope and resolution without employing decomposition techniques.
transmission line and storage charge/discharge losses are not defined, so "unphysical" energy destruction does not need to be mitigated against.
User-defined constraints are necessary to represent policy targets (e.g. systemwide limits, possibly only affecting a subset of technologies).
Users require a GUI to navigate model preparation, optimisation, and analysis.
The gas distribution network is resolved alongside the electricity transmission network.
Transmission between regions is represented using DC optimal power flow.

useCases.name: Network Development Plan (NDP) / Transmission Planning Process (TPP)
useCases.description: Create a set of detailed scenarios of e.g., 2050 transmission grid designs for use in guiding policy implementation and providing boundary conditions for investors, utilities, and local authorities to develop their own plans. The transmission plans will be optimized based on high-level scenarios of decarbonised energy system findings.
assumptions: The optimization will be run with perfect foresight over the full model horizon, which spans multiple years/decades.
Generator capacities are fixed by the integrated resource plan (IRP) at each of the model investment years.
Assets are grouped and only their dispatch, not their unit commitment is represented.
Contracted operating arrangements and regulated limits (e.g. on emissions) defined in the IRP are applied.
Non-linear transmission characteristics need to be defined, using piecewise linearisation.
Transmission between zones is represented using AC optimal power flow.
The transmission network is accurately represented, albeit aggregated into larger zones.
Transmission limits are defined by power limits (grid transfer capacities).
There is sufficient computational capacity to run the model with defined spatio-temporal scope and resolution without employing decomposition techniques.
Investment and storage asset horizon edge effects are ignored.
The system supply-demand balance is relaxed. Load shedding is limited with constraints on EENS and LOLP applied alongside a value of lost load (VOLL).
User-defined decision variables may be required to enable one-off transmission system quirks to be suitably constrained.
Users require a GUI to navigate model preparation, optimisation, and analysis.
Different weather and demand years are used to stress-test the model but not as a formal Monte Carlo analysis.
The output data must be formatted appropriately for regulatory approval.

useCases.name: Policy Target Setting
useCases.description: Political exercise to set carbon emission pathways to meet future year targets
assumptions: The optimization will be run with perfect foresight over the full model horizon, which spans multiple decades at 5 year resolution.
Spatial scope is national and single node. Could be multinode at national resolution if multinational but not chosen here.
Year is represented by representative time slices (heuristics: day/night/peak/season). Could also be representative periods based on automated timeseries clustering, but not chosen here.
Storage aggregated. Need mathematical representation to handle inter-slice storage.
Assets are always grouped.
Sub-group assets by their costs/resource (pre-processed). Includes e.g. wind techs, sources of fuels etc. Group assets back up in postprocessing.
User constraints/variables are necessary to limit total emissions etc. for subsets of the system being defined.
No representation of complex asset characteristics.
Flexible demand is necessary.
Endogenous learning (piecewise investment cost) not used as it distorts the model.
Grid-transfer capacities used for multi-node models.
Multi-carrier, including electricity, hydrogen, natural gas, heat, etc.
Demands are end-use services (e.g. "vehicle kms" for transport demands).
Extraction of fossils are represented as assets, competing with e.g. imports.
Sensitivity scenarios will be conducted but detailed sensitivity analysis/stochastic optimisation is beyond the scope of this study.
Outages represented by a reserve margin of dispatchable capacity. Assets also have an availability factor.
GUI is necessary, particularly for outputs.
Marginal/shadow prices required to compare market prices between scenarios.
Technology-specific discount rates are used to represent consumer preferences on payback periods (a.k.a. hurdle rates).
Demand elasticity is represented in loads.

useCases.name: Asset portfolio investment plan
useCases.description: Create an asset portfolio investment plan as a private / public utility company. This plan will be guided by national / regional plans (IRPs, NDPs, etc.), the company's   current risk appetite, and any upcoming changes to market mechanisms / subsidies which may impact revenue.
assumptions: The optimization will be run over individual years both with perfect foresight (capacity planning) and with myopic foresight over days or weeks within the year (operating revenue analysis).
Financial and operational horizon edge effects must be considered as the portfolio includes storage devices.
No timeseries simplification is undertaken because the spatial and generator scope is limited to cover only the assets in the portfolio.
The rest of the system develops according to the scenarios set out by the integrated resource plan (IRP) and network development plan (NDP) and is resolved coarsely.
Portfolio assets are resolved individually with unit commitment characteristics (ramp rate, up/down-time, etc.) and non-linear operating and financial considerations that are piecewise linearised.
Hydro cascading is represented, as well as asset linking within power plants, where those power plants have multiple possible asset configurations.
Transmission from assets to the rest of the system is represented using AC optimal power flow, is limited by PTDF and considers phase angles.
Available investment limits the total capacity of new assets that can be feasibly purchased.
Weather and market uncertainties are mitigated against using two-stage stochastic optimisation.
Externalities (loads, changes to asset capacities beyond the current portfolio) must be forecast over the next 10-15 years.

Profit-maximisation must be represented in how the portfolio is committed and dispatched in the day-ahead and intra-day markets, which requires competitors and their perceived risk appetite to be resolved.
